title: Recursion
subject: Programming
prompt: Explain recursion using the factorial function as an example. Describe the base case, the recursive case, how the calls build up and unwind, and what happens without a base case.

points.statement: A recursive function solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of the same problem.
points.hint: Say that the function calls itself on a smaller input.

points.statement: The base case stops the recursion: factorial(0) or factorial(1) returns 1 without another call.
points.hint: Name the base case and what it returns.

points.statement: The recursive case computes n! as n multiplied by (n - 1)!.
Each call waits on the call stack; when the base case returns, the calls unwind and multiply the results back up.
points.hint: Describe the call stack and the unwinding.

points.statement: Without a base case the calls never stop, causing infinite recursion and a stack overflow.
points.hint: Explain what happens with no base case.

points.statement: Recursion uses extra memory for each call compared with a loop.

trap.false_claim: Recursion uses no more memory than a loop, because the computer reuses the same variables.
trap.truth: Every recursive call adds a frame to the call stack, so memory grows with the depth of the recursion.

probe.kp1: In your own words, what makes a function recursive?
probe.kp2: What is the base case for factorial, and why does it matter?
probe.kp3: How would you write factorial(n) in terms of a smaller factorial?
probe.kp4: Walk me through what happens on the call stack for factorial(3).
probe.kp5: What would happen if factorial had no base case?
probe.kp6: How is the recursive factorial different from one written with a loop?

follow_ups.what_if: What happens if someone calls your factorial with a negative number?
